title: Cryo-EM structure of a 95-base-pair double-stranded DNA minicircle at 5.3 A resolution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the deposited coordinate file PDB 13GQ (449 KB mmCIF, a text format for atomic coordinates): it contains exactly 3,895 atoms in 2 chains of 95 residues each. Every residue in chain A is DA (deoxyadenosine) and every residue in chain B is DT (deoxythymidine), i.e. a generic poly(A:T) placeholder rather than the real synthesised sequence; the PDB entry title itself says 'poly(A:T) model'. Also pulled the RCSB entry metadata (5.27 A resolution, 344,629 particles, single class) and the EMDB EMD-77061 entry metadata, and did a HEAD request on the cryo-EM density map (258 MB gzipped, so not downloaded, over the 50 MB cap).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The nine-fold periodicity in helical twist, ~10.56 base pairs per turn, groove-width analysis, ellipticity and out-of-plane displacement numbers, and the actual oligonucleotide sequences (stated to be in Supporting Information section S1.1). The Europe PMC supplementary-file listing timed out twice, so the supplement is not retrievable and I could not confirm whether per-base-pair-step geometry tables are tabulated there.

a1_downloadable.note: PDB 13GQ coordinates and EMDB EMD-77061 map are public with no login. I fetched the mmCIF coordinate file successfully; the 258 MB map was confirmed present by HEAD but left undownloaded.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no label column anywhere. The quantities the paper reports (helical twist per base-pair step, groove widths, ellipticity) exist only as figures in the text; to get them you would have to run a geometry program such as 3DNA or Curves+ over the coordinates yourself, i.e. construct the target.

a3_inputs_present.note: The obvious input for any DNA-shape task is the base sequence, and it is absent from the deposited model: all 95 residues of chain A are adenine and all 95 of chain B are thymine, a fabricated placeholder because bases cannot be distinguished at 5.3 A. The real sequence is only in a supplement I could not retrieve.

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates are in Angstroms and B-factors (a per-atom measure of positional uncertainty, range 20.0-433.6) are standard mmCIF fields with defined units. Units are not the problem here.

a5_enough_rows.note: One structure. At best 95 base pairs, or 94-95 base-pair steps, all from a single molecule in a single conformational class. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows; this is two orders of magnitude short, and the rows are not even independent since they come from one fitted model.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.45 MB coordinates; 258 MB gzipped density map if ever needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small. Size is the one thing this candidate has going for it.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper says 95 base pairs and 5.3 A; the deposited file has exactly 95 residues per strand and RCSB metadata reports 5.27 A. Counts agree.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any target (twist, roll, groove width) is computed geometrically from the same atomic coordinates that would serve as the features, which is leakage by construction. Worse, those coordinates are themselves a flexibly fitted model at 5.3 A where individual bases are unresolved, so the per-step geometry is partly an artefact of the fitting restraints, not a direct measurement.

existing_models.name: Deep DNAshape (Li, Rohs and colleagues; Nature Communications 2024, with a 2024 Nucleic Acids Research webserver paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts 14 DNA shape features from sequence, including helical twist and minor groove width, accounting for flanking regions up to 7 base pairs; trained on Monte Carlo and molecular-dynamics simulation data. I retrieved the papers but did not read out a specific held-out accuracy number, so I am not quoting one.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Their stated gap is that training rests on limited simulation data rather than experimental structures, and that conformational flexibility/fluctuation prediction is the harder, less validated part.

existing_models.name: CryoREAD and EM2NA (deep-learning builders of DNA/RNA atomic models from cryo-EM density maps)
existing_models.score_and_split: EM2NA reports 83.15% residue coverage, 1.06 A C4' root-mean-square deviation and 46.86% sequence recall on maps better than 5 A; CryoREAD is a published U-Net tool with open code. Numbers are from the retrieved abstracts.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Sequence assignment from density remains poor (under 50% recall), which is exactly why this paper modelled a poly(A:T) placeholder.

backbone.name: None applicable. DNA language models (DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer, HyenaDNA) take sequence, and no usable sequence is in the deposited data.
backbone.licence: PDB and EMDB depositions are CC0 / public domain, so licence is not the blocker.

integration.partner_dataset: In principle PDB/NDB (Nucleic Acid Database) DNA structures joinable on PDB ID, or Deep DNAshape's simulation-derived shape tables joinable on sequence k-mer.
integration.join_key: PDB ID (for structures) or base sequence (for shape tables) - but the sequence is a fabricated poly(A:T) in this entry, so the sequence join is void.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not write one that this single structure contributes to: with 95 base-pair steps from one molecule it adds a data point to a comparison, not a training signal to a model.

controls.positive_control: None possible with n=1 structure; there is no held-out set to recover a known effect in.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless on 95 correlated steps from one fitted model.
controls.external_validation: Other DNA structures exist (the paper itself compares to PDB 1RVH, 1RVI and 1KX5, the last being the nucleosome), but they would be the dataset, not a validation of anything learned here.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is available from this paper's data: a single 95-base-pair cryo-EM structure, deposited as a sequence-free poly(A:T) model at 5.3 A, can support a structural-biology observation about DNA bending under topological constraint but cannot train or test a predictor.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA base sequence to predict how a closed DNA ring twists and how wide its grooves are.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on per-base-pair-step geometry from circular DNA structures. This paper supplies exactly one structure, 95 base pairs, 3,895 atoms, with no real sequence attached - a number I verified in the deposited coordinate file.
plain_idea.predict: Helical twist angle and major/minor groove width at each base-pair step. The ground truth would come from running a nucleic-acid geometry program over atomic coordinates fitted into a cryo-electron-microscopy density map at 5.3 A resolution.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups designing DNA nanostructures and people studying extrachromosomal circular DNA in cancer would want sequence-level predictions of where a small ring strains or kinks. But that needs hundreds of structures, and this paper is one.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict sequence-dependent helical twist and groove width in topologically constrained (circular) DNA from base sequence, using this minicircle as experimental ground truth to test whether simulation-trained predictors like Deep DNAshape transfer to bent DNA. The idea is reasonable but this paper cannot supply the data - one structure, no sequence in the model, and geometry that must be derived from the same coordinates that would be the features. A viable version would mine the whole Nucleic Acid Database / PDB set of DNA structures, which is a different project with a different source.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the actual download and parse: the coordinate file is 449 KB and parsed in under a second with a 40-line Python script. Compute was never the constraint; sample size was.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the residues in the deposited coordinate file and look at what bases they are. That took one script: 95 adenines in chain A, 95 thymines in chain B, one structure, no real sequence. Project dead in five minutes.

verdict_reason: A single cryo-EM structure is not a dataset. Verified in the deposited file (PDB 13GQ): 3,895 atoms, two 95-residue strands, and crucially every base is a placeholder - chain A is all adenine, chain B is all thymine, because at 5.3 A resolution the real sequence cannot be read out. That kills A3 (the natural input, sequence, is absent and fabricated), A5 (95 non-independent base-pair steps against a ~1,500-row floor), A2 (the geometric targets are not a column; they would have to be computed with 3DNA or Curves+) and A8 (those targets would be computed from the same coordinates used as features, and from a flexibly fitted low-resolution model at that). This is a fine structural-biology result with real value as one comparison point for DNA bending, and Deep DNAshape already occupies the sequence-to-shape prediction niche using simulation data. There is no ML project here.
